reference_answer:
Let S={I,X,Y,Z} and T=(1/4) sum over P in S of P*rho*P^dagger. Each of these four matrices is Hermitian and unitary, so this is the operator in the question. For Q in {X,Y,Z}, the conjugation expansion is Q*T*Q^dagger=(1/4) sum_P (Q*P)*rho*(Q*P)^dagger. The rightmost factor is P^dagger*Q^dagger=P*Q, not Q*P. Products of distinct Hermitian Paulis need not themselves be Hermitian, so that adjoint cannot be dropped.

Left multiplication by Q permutes the four Pauli classes modulo scalar phases. More explicitly, for each P there are a unit-modulus scalar omega_P and a uniquely associated R_P in S such that Q*P=omega_P*R_P, and P->R_P is a permutation. In each conjugation term the scalar cancels with its complex conjugate: (omega_P R_P)*rho*(omega_P R_P)^dagger=R_P*rho*R_P^dagger. Relabeling this finite sum therefore proves Q*T*Q^dagger=T. Since Q is unitary, multiplying on the right by Q gives Q*T=T*Q. The same follows for all products of the generators and scalar central phases, so T commutes with the irreducible Pauli representation.

Now use Schur's commutant-is-scalars corollary on the finite-dimensional complex space C^2: T=lambda*I. The hypotheses needed for its scalar conclusion are present, not silently assumed for a general field or an infinite-dimensional representation. Cyclicity of trace and P^dagger*P=I give tr(P*rho*P^dagger)=tr(rho)=1 for every P. Thus tr(T)=1. On the other hand tr(lambda*I)=2*lambda, so lambda=1/2 and T=I/2. This follows from conjugation invariance, irreducibility and trace normalization, without computing the entries of rho. Positivity supplies the density-state interpretation but is not needed for the linear-operator identity T(A)=tr(A)*I/2. That extension is a mathematical consequence of the same proof, not a newly compiled local Lean theorem or a circuit-resource claim.

rubric.criterion: Expands Q*T*Q^dagger with right factor (QP)^dagger=PQ, then uses a bijection of Pauli classes modulo unit phases and adjoint phase cancellation. Does not treat every product QP as Hermitian.
Derives commutation with the whole representation and applies the scalar commutant corollary on finite-dimensional C^2 with the given irreducibility.
Uses trace cyclicity and P^dagger*P=I to get tr(T)=1=2*lambda and lambda=1/2.
Concludes T=I/2 for every input density matrix by the Schur/averaging argument, not brute-force coordinates or a new formal/circuit claim.

exposition.core_summary: Pauli conjugation permutes operator-conjugation terms modulo phases only when the right adjoint is retained; Schur and trace then give the maximally mixed output on C^2.

semantic_steps.claim: Each P in {I,X,Y,Z} is Hermitian-unitary, so P*rho*P^dagger=P*rho*P; a scalar phase cancels only against its adjoint phase.
Q*T*Q^dagger=(1/4)sum_P (QP)*rho*(QP)^dagger; QP permutes the Pauli classes modulo unit phases, so the correctly conjugated sum is T.
Unitary Q then gives Q*T=T*Q, and hence commutation with the entire irreducible Pauli representation.
The scalar Schur corollary applies on finite-dimensional C^2 and gives T=lambda*I.
Cyclicity gives tr(T)=1=2*lambda, so T=I/2 independently of the density matrix entries.
